sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Many scientists who study people end up saying some version of the following sentence.
sentences.zh: 许多研究人类的科学家最终都会说出类似下面这句话的结论。

sentences.en: The human being is the only animal that
sentences.zh: 人类是唯一一种

sentences.en: has a sense of humor.
sentences.zh: 拥有幽默感的动物。

sentences.en: That can cooperate.
sentences.zh: 能够合作的动物。

sentences.en: That do radio shows.
sentences.zh: 会做广播节目的动物。

sentences.en: That regularly fashion and use tools.
sentences.zh: 会定期制作并使用工具的动物。

sentences.en: That have chins.
sentences.zh: 长着下巴的动物。

sentences.en: Psychologist Daniel Gilbert at Harvard University finishes the sentence this way.
sentences.zh: 哈佛大学的心理学家丹尼尔·吉尔伯特是这样总结这句话的。

sentences.en: The human being is the only animal that thinks about the future.
sentences.zh: 人类是唯一一种会思考未来的动物。

sentences.en: Every animal learns from trial and error.
sentences.zh: 每种动物都会通过试错来学习。

sentences.en: Human beings learn from experiences they've never even had.
sentences.zh: 而人类可以从从未经历过的事情中学习。

sentences.en: They close their eyes and say,
sentences.zh: 他们闭上眼睛，心想：

sentences.en: Would I like liver and onion ice cream?
sentences.zh: 我会喜欢吃洋葱肝脏味的冰淇淋吗？

sentences.en: Yuck.
sentences.zh: 真恶心。

sentences.en: Would it be a good idea to put my finger in a pencil sharpener?
sentences.zh: 把手指伸进卷笔刀里是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不是。

sentences.en: But just because we humans have great imaginations,
sentences.zh: 但仅仅因为我们人类拥有伟大的想象力，

sentences.en: it doesn't mean we do a good job of predicting the future accurately.
sentences.zh: 并不意味着我们能准确地预测未来。

sentences.en: People just aren't very good at looking into their future
sentences.zh: 人们并不擅长审视自己的未来，

sentences.en: and predicting correctly their emotional reactions
sentences.zh: 也无法正确预测自己对

sentences.en: to the events that might unfold.
sentences.zh: 未来可能发生的事件的情绪反应。

sentences.en: We think a dentist appointment will be awful,
sentences.zh: 我们以为看牙医会很糟糕，

sentences.en: and then it's not so bad.
sentences.zh: 结果却没那么糟。

sentences.en: We think buying a new car will make us very happy,
sentences.zh: 我们以为买辆新车会让我们非常开心，

sentences.en: but it ends up being just nice.
sentences.zh: 结果却觉得也就那样。

sentences.en: We think losing a job is the worst thing that could happen to us,
sentences.zh: 我们以为失业是可能发生在我们身上最糟糕的事，

sentences.en: and then it becomes the best thing.
sentences.zh: 结果它反而成了最好的事。

sentences.en: The problem is, once our minds get to work imagining the future,
sentences.zh: 问题在于，一旦我们的大脑开始想象未来，

sentences.en: we leave out lots of details,
sentences.zh: 我们就会忽略很多细节，

sentences.en: like the nice lady at the front desk at the dentist's office
sentences.zh: 比如牙医诊所前台那位友好的女士，

sentences.en: or the free toothbrush.
sentences.zh: 或者免费的牙刷。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain,
sentences.zh: 本周的《隐藏的大脑》节目，

sentences.en: we confront how little we actually understand about what we want,
sentences.zh: 我们将直面我们对自己想要什么了解得有多么少，

sentences.en: and we try to figure out how we can make future versions of ourselves happier.
sentences.zh: 并试图找出如何让未来的自己更快乐的方法。

sentences.en: It continues our annual summer series, U2.0.
sentences.zh: 这是我们年度夏季系列节目“U2.0”的延续。

sentences.en: Authenticity is contagious.
sentences.zh: 真实感是会传染的。

sentences.en: I've been dragged into this all the way, kicking and screaming.
sentences.zh: 我被一路拖进了这个过程，又踢又叫。

sentences.en: Ideas and advice about how you can respond to life's chaos.
sentences.zh: 关于如何应对生活混乱的观点和建议。

sentences.en: Let me just do a just check to my inbox.
sentences.zh: 让我先检查一下我的收件箱。

sentences.en: Just check.
sentences.zh: 就检查一下。

sentences.en: Just check.
sentences.zh: 就检查一下。

sentences.en: Just check to my phone real quick.
sentences.zh: 快速检查一下我的手机。

sentences.en: With wisdom.
sentences.zh: 带着智慧。

sentences.en: Daniel Gilbert is a psychology professor at Harvard University.
sentences.zh: 丹尼尔·吉尔伯特是哈佛大学的心理学教授。

sentences.en: He's the author of the book, Stumbling on Happiness,
sentences.zh: 他是《撞上幸福》一书的作者，

sentences.en: and he's one of my favorite researchers in the world.
sentences.zh: 也是我世界上最喜欢的科研人员之一。

sentences.en: Dan, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 丹，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: Well, thank you.
sentences.zh: 嗯，谢谢你。

sentences.en: You're now my favorite radio host in the world.
sentences.zh: 你现在是我世界上最喜欢的广播主持人了。

sentences.en: Well, that was easy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这可真容易。

sentences.en: I want to start by asking you a question that you and I talked about a while ago, Dan.
sentences.zh: 我想先问你一个你我之前讨论过的问题，丹。

sentences.en: Some years ago, you went through a series of very difficult personal experiences,
sentences.zh: 几年前，你经历了一系列非常艰难的个人事件，

sentences.en: but instead of leaving you brokenhearted, as you might have anticipated,
sentences.zh: 但正如你可能预料的那样，这些经历并没有让你心碎，

sentences.en: it left you with actually a very important insight into your own ability to predict your future emotional states.
sentences.zh: 反而让你对自己预测未来情绪状态的能力有了非常重要的洞察。

sentences.en: Can you tell me what happened?
sentences.zh: 你能告诉我发生了什么吗？

sentences.en: Well, you know, my personal experiences were no worse than the average person's, in fact, better than moSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，我的个人经历并不比普通人更糟糕，事实上，比大多数人都要好。

sentences.en: But, you know, like everybody, I suffer the slings and arrows of outrageous fortune.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，像每个人一样，我承受着命运无情的打击。

sentences.en: You know, we have divorces.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们经历离婚。

sentences.en: We have surgeries.
sentences.zh: 我们经历手术。

sentences.en: We have breakups with women we love and friends we enjoy.
sentences.zh: 我们与深爱的人和喜欢的友人们分手。

sentences.en: So it was sort of ordinary events that befell me all in one year.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些发生在我身上的一切，在一年之内，其实都是些寻常事件。

sentences.en: And I realized that had you asked me a year earlier how I would be faring,
sentences.zh: 我意识到，如果你在一年前问我我会过得怎么样，

sentences.en: the answer would have been, oh, my gosh, I'll be devastated.
sentences.zh: 我的回答会是，天哪，我会崩溃的。

sentences.en: But I wasn't devastated.
sentences.zh: 但我并没有崩溃。

sentences.en: It wasn't a good year, but it was okay.
sentences.zh: 那一年过得并不好，但还过得去。

sentences.en: And it made me wonder if I was the only person who was just too stupid to be able to look ahead into his future
sentences.zh: 这让我怀疑，是不是只有我一个人太蠢，无法预见自己的未来，

sentences.en: and figure out how he'd feel if really bad or maybe really good things happened.
sentences.zh: 也无法弄清楚如果发生非常糟糕或非常好的事情时，自己会有什么感觉。

sentences.en: So I went to the laboratory and teamed up with my friend Tim Wilson, and we started studying this phenomenon.
sentences.zh: 所以我去了实验室，和我的朋友蒂姆·威尔逊合作，我们开始研究这种现象。

sentences.en: And, you know, reassuringly, we found out we weren't the only stupid people out there.
sentences.zh: 而且，令人欣慰的是，我们发现我们并不是唯一愚蠢的人。

sentences.en: You've also found that painful decisions are often painful largely because we haven't made them yet.
sentences.zh: 你还发现，痛苦的决定之所以痛苦，很大程度上是因为我们还没做出决定。

sentences.en: Once we actually make a decision, pick one of two alternatives,
sentences.zh: 一旦我们真正做出了决定，在两个选项中选了一个，

sentences.en: we often end up wondering how we could ever have dreamed of choosing the other choice.
sentences.zh: 我们往往最终会纳闷自己当初怎么会想到选另一个选项。

sentences.en: Well, surely that's true for all of us.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对我们所有人来说肯定都是真的。

sentences.en: We agonize between two things that seem awfully close.
sentences.zh: 我们在两个看起来非常接近的事情之间纠结。

sentences.en: We finally choose one, and in a small or medium amount of time,
sentences.zh: 我们最终选择了其中一个，在一段时间后，

sentences.en: we look back and wonder how we could ever have been trying to decide between them.
sentences.zh: 我们回过头来，纳闷自己当初怎么会纠结于它们之间。

sentences.en: Why did we make that mistake of thinking the two alternatives were so close when, in fact, they were really far apart?
sentences.zh: 为什么我们会犯下那种认为两个选项如此接近的错误，而事实上，它们相差甚远？

sentences.en: The answer is they weren't really close, and they weren't really far apart.
sentences.zh: 答案是它们并不真的接近，也不真的相差甚远。

sentences.en: It's just a matter of how you look at it.
sentences.zh: 这只是你看待它的方式问题。

sentences.en: And when you're on the front side of a decision, alternatives seem to be very close.
sentences.zh: 当你处于决策的前期时，选项看起来非常接近。

sentences.en: But once you've chosen one, the mind gets going doing what the mind does so well,
sentences.zh: 但一旦你选择了其中一个，大脑就会开始做它最擅长的事，

sentences.en: convincing you that the thing you've got is better than the thing you've left behind.
sentences.zh: 说服你，你拥有的东西比你放弃的东西更好。

sentences.en: Now, if psychologists are trying to cure that, we call it rationalization.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果心理学家试图治愈这种心理，我们称之为合理化。

sentences.en: If we're trying to sell it, we call it coping.
sentences.zh: 如果我们试图推销它，我们称之为应对。

sentences.en: But whether you call it coping or rationalization, it's the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但无论你称之为应对还是合理化，它们都是一回事。

sentences.en: It's the mind-finding realistic ways to see the world so that it feels better about the world in which it finds itself.
sentences.zh: 这是大脑在寻找现实的方式来看待世界，以便让自己对所处的世界感觉更好。

sentences.en: You once subscribed to the very popular belief that I think I still subscribe to,
sentences.zh: 你曾经信奉一个非常流行的观点，我想我至今仍信奉，

sentences.en: that more freedom always equals more happiness.
sentences.zh: 即更多的自由总是等于更多的幸福。

sentences.en: And if I remember correctly, you conducted a study once that found that this wasn't quite right.
sentences.zh: 如果我没记错的话，你曾经做过一项研究，发现事实并非完全如此。

sentences.en: And at the time, I think you told me that you'd been living with your girlfriend for more than a decade,
sentences.zh: 当时，我想你告诉我，你和你的女朋友已经同居了十多年，

sentences.en: and you saw the data, and you decided to make some changes in your life.
sentences.zh: 你看到了数据，于是决定改变一下自己的生活。

sentences.en: You have a very good memory.
sentences.zh: 你的记性真好。

sentences.en: So like many people, I used to believe that the more freedom, the better.
sentences.zh: 所以像许多人一样，我过去也认为自由越多越好。

sentences.en: How could you be less happy when you had more choice?
sentences.zh: 当你拥有更多选择时，怎么可能不那么快乐呢？

sentences.en: Well, we know now a lot about why more choice sometimes makes people less happy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们现在很清楚为什么更多的选择有时会让人们不那么快乐。

sentences.en: In our study, we brought students in, and we created a photography course,
sentences.zh: 在我们的研究中，我们请来了一些学生，开设了一门摄影课程，

sentences.en: and we had all of them work with us for a long time, learning how to do black-and-white photography.
sentences.zh: 我们让他们所有人都和我们一起工作了很长时间，学习如何进行黑白摄影。

sentences.en: Then at the end of the course, we gave them two photographs that they had taken,
sentences.zh: 然后在课程结束时，我们给了他们两张他们拍摄的照片，

sentences.en: and we said they could keep one, and we were going to keep one.
sentences.zh: 我们说他们可以留下一张，而我们要留下一张。

sentences.en: Well, this was horrible for them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这对他们来说太痛苦了。

sentences.en: They wanted to keep both.
sentences.zh: 他们想两张都留下。

sentences.en: They had a tough decision to make.
sentences.zh: 他们必须做出一个艰难的决定。

sentences.en: In one group, we said, if you ever change your mind about which photograph you want,
sentences.zh: 在其中一组，我们说，如果你改变了主意，想要换另一张照片，

sentences.en: just let us know.
sentences.zh: 随时告诉我们。

sentences.en: We'll swap with you.
sentences.zh: 我们会和你交换。

sentences.en: We're going to keep this on file forever.
sentences.zh: 我们会把这张照片存档，永久保留。

sentences.en: So if you took A and you want B, we'll swap B for A, for as long as we both shall live.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你选了A，但想要B，只要我们还活着，我们就会为你交换。

sentences.en: Another group was told, your decision is final.
sentences.zh: 另一组被告知，你的决定是最终的。

sentences.en: Once you make this decision, the photograph that you're donating to us gets sent off to England.
sentences.zh: 一旦你做出这个决定，你捐给我们的那张照片就会被送到英国。

sentences.en: It'll never be seen again.
sentences.zh: 它将永远不会再被看到。

sentences.en: And, of course, if you presented those choices to me, I would say I would want to be in the first group
sentences.zh: 当然，如果你把这些选择摆在我面前，我会说我想成为第一组的人，

sentences.en: because I would preserve my options.
sentences.zh: 因为我想保留我的选择权。

sentences.en: If I took a photograph home and didn't like it, I could come back and trade it in for the one that I did like.
sentences.zh: 如果我把照片带回家后不喜欢，我可以回来换成我喜欢的那张。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And that's not even just a good guess.
sentences.zh: 这甚至不仅仅是一个好的猜测。

sentences.en: We actually did exactly that in another study.
sentences.zh: 我们在另一项研究中确实做了完全相同的事情。

sentences.en: We asked people which group they wanted to be in, and just like you,
sentences.zh: 我们问人们想成为哪一组的人，就像你一样，

sentences.en: they overwhelmingly want to be in the first group.
sentences.zh: 他们绝大多数人都想成为第一组。

sentences.en: But what's interesting is we tracked the happiness of the people who had made these decisions
sentences.zh: 但有趣的是，我们追踪了那些做出这些决定的人的幸福感，

sentences.en: over the course of several weeks.
sentences.zh: 持续了几个星期。

sentences.en: And what we found is that people who made an irrevocable decision, one they couldn't change,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些做出不可撤销决定的人，即他们无法改变决定的人，

sentences.en: were much happier with the choice they made.
sentences.zh: 对他们所做的选择要快乐得多。

sentences.en: When you've made an irrevocable decision, you rationalize it.
sentences.zh: 当你做出一个不可撤销的决定时，你会合理化它。

sentences.en: Once something's gone and gone forever, the mind gets to work figuring out why
sentences.zh: 一旦某样东西永远消失了，大脑就会开始工作，弄清楚为什么

sentences.en: what it got is really better than what it loSt.
sentences.zh: 它所得到的东西确实比它失去的东西更好。

sentences.en: But when a decision isn't irrevocable, when you can remake it and revisit it and change your mind anytime,
sentences.zh: 但当一个决定不是不可撤销的，当你随时可以重新做出决定、重新审视并改变主意时，

sentences.en: what do you do?
sentences.zh: 你会怎么做？

sentences.en: You just ruminate about it, right?
sentences.zh: 你只会反复琢磨它，对吧？

sentences.en: You buy a sweater and you know you can take it back anytime, and every time you put it on,
sentences.zh: 你买了一件毛衣，你知道你可以随时退货，每次你穿上它时，

sentences.en: you look in the mirror and you think, I don't know, maybe it's not a good fit.
sentences.zh: 你照照镜子，心想，我不知道，也许它不太合身。

sentences.en: Maybe it's not a good color.
sentences.zh: 也许颜色不太好。

sentences.en: Maybe I ought to bring it back.
sentences.zh: 也许我应该把它退回去。

sentences.en: On the other hand, if this sweater was bought at a place that won't take it back,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，如果这件毛衣是在一家不接受退货的店里买的，

sentences.en: you look in the mirror and you say, gosh, that looks good.
sentences.zh: 你照照镜子，会说，天哪，这看起来真不错。

sentences.en: So you took this research and you applied it to your own life.
sentences.zh: 所以你采用了这项研究，并将其应用到了你自己的生活中。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 我确实这么做了。

sentences.en: I think my then-girlfriend and I had been living together for about a decade.
sentences.zh: 我想我和当时的女朋友已经同居了大约十年。

sentences.en: And once we saw the results of this experiment, and a friend of mine, Dave Myers, called and said,
sentences.zh: 当我们看到这个实验的结果时，我的朋友戴夫·迈尔斯打电话来说，

sentences.en: you know, I think this really explains the difference between living together and getting married,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这真的解释了同居和结婚之间的区别，

sentences.en: which had never occurred to me.
sentences.zh: 这我以前从未想到过。

sentences.en: I thought, you know, if you're a scientist and you don't live by your own results,
sentences.zh: 我想，你知道，如果你是一名科学家，却不按照自己的研究结果生活，

sentences.en: what kind of scientist are you?
sentences.zh: 那你算什么科学家？

sentences.en: So, yeah, I went home and proposed.
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，我回家求婚了。

sentences.en: And guess what?
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着？

sentences.en: But I was utterly right.
sentences.zh: 但我完全是对的。

sentences.en: I love her so much more now that we're married, now that I can't get out of this relationship
sentences.zh: 我现在比结婚前更爱她了，因为现在我无法逃离这段关系，

sentences.en: no matter how fast I run.
sentences.zh: 无论我跑得有多快。

sentences.en: She is the love of my life.
sentences.zh: 她是我一生的挚爱。

sentences.en: And I didn't realize that when I was always thinking, should I stay or shouldn't I stay?
sentences.zh: 当时我总是纠结于“我该留下还是离开”，却没意识到这一点。

sentences.en: There's a lot to be said for making commitments.
sentences.zh: 做出承诺有很多值得称道的地方。

sentences.en: So let's talk a little bit about why these errors often happen.
sentences.zh: 那么，我们来聊聊为什么这些错误经常发生。

sentences.en: One idea that you've explored is that when we imagine the future,
sentences.zh: 你探索过一个观点，即当我们想象未来时，

sentences.en: we often fail to take into account all the little details that will actually make us happy or sad.
sentences.zh: 我们往往忽略了那些真正会让我们感到快乐或悲伤的细枝末节。

sentences.en: Well, it's true.
sentences.zh: 嗯，确实如此。

sentences.en: Every future event comprises thousands and thousands of details.
sentences.zh: 每一个未来的事件都包含成千上万个细节。

sentences.en: But when you ask people to imagine a future event,
sentences.zh: 但当你让人们想象一个未来事件时，

sentences.en: they usually imagine one or two of those details,
sentences.zh: 他们通常只会想象其中一两个细节，

sentences.en: the ones that are central, that define the episode.
sentences.zh: 那些核心的、定义了该事件的细节。

sentences.en: So if I say to you, imagine the next visit to the dentist,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我对你说，想象一下下次去看牙医的情景，

sentences.en: probably you get a picture in your head instantly of sitting in a chair
sentences.zh: 你脑海中立刻浮现的画面可能就是坐在椅子上，

sentences.en: and someone's fooling around in your mouth.
sentences.zh: 有人在你的嘴里摆弄。

sentences.en: Well, that is indeed a part of the experience you'll have.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那确实是你将要经历的一部分体验。

sentences.en: But you also have to park.
sentences.zh: 但你还得停车。

sentences.en: You're also going to be in the waiting room.
sentences.zh: 你还得在候诊室等待。

sentences.en: They're going to be playing music.
sentences.zh: 他们会播放音乐。

sentences.en: There will be magazines.
sentences.zh: 会有杂志看。

sentences.en: The receptionist will be nice or not.
sentences.zh: 前台接待员可能态度好，也可能不好。

sentences.en: Afterwards, you will or won't have an appointment you need to rush to.
sentences.zh: 事后，你可能还要赶去赴另一个约，也可能不用。

sentences.en: There's lots of other parts of that experience that you're not imagining.
sentences.zh: 那段经历中还有很多你没有想象到的部分。

sentences.en: And all of them can affect your happiness.
sentences.zh: 而所有这些都可能影响你的幸福感。

sentences.en: Now, you can't imagine every detail.
sentences.zh: 当然，你不可能想象出每一个细节。

sentences.en: That's not possible.
sentences.zh: 那是不可能的。

sentences.en: But what you ought to do rationally is think to yourself,
sentences.zh: 但理性的做法是告诉自己：

sentences.en: I'm only imagining one or two of the many pieces of the experience.
sentences.zh: 我只是在想象这段经历中众多片段里的一两个。

sentences.en: And as a result, I should be very humble about my prediction.
sentences.zh: 因此，对于自己的预测，我应该保持谦逊。

sentences.en: But nobody is.
sentences.zh: 但没人会这么做。

sentences.en: Instead, they say, a dental visit?
sentences.zh: 相反，他们会说，看牙医？

sentences.en: I'll hate it.
sentences.zh: 我肯定会讨厌它。

sentences.en: One of the most interesting things you found in this line of research is that
sentences.zh: 你在这一系列研究中发现的最有趣的现象之一是，

sentences.en: it's not just that we don't imagine the event in the future in all its fullness and detail.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅没有全面细致地想象未来的事件，

sentences.en: We also don't fully appreciate that we might not quite be the same people we are then that we are now.
sentences.zh: 我们也没有充分意识到，未来的我们可能与现在的我们并不完全相同。

sentences.en: You know, I think that's even the more powerful of the two errors.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为这才是这两个错误中更严重的一个。

sentences.en: So you're quite right.
sentences.zh: 你说得非常对。

sentences.en: One problem is that we don't imagine events correctly.
sentences.zh: 一个问题是我们没有正确地想象事件。

sentences.en: We don't imagine them as they will unfold.
sentences.zh: 我们没有按它们实际展开的样子去想象。

sentences.en: That's the smaller of the two probleMs.
sentences.zh: 这是两个问题中较小的一个。

sentences.en: The larger problem is that we don't know who we will be when we are experiencing that event.
sentences.zh: 更大的问题是，我们不知道当真正经历那个事件时，我们会变成什么样的人。

sentences.en: We underestimate the mind's ability to react to events in a different way than it's reacting to them in prospect.
sentences.zh: 我们低估了大脑在经历事件时，与在预想事件时做出不同反应的能力。

sentences.en: You know, things look different from out the windshield and in the rearview mirror.
sentences.zh: 你知道，透过挡风玻璃看前方和通过后视镜看后方，景象是不同的。

sentences.en: Life is like that, too.
sentences.zh: 生活也是如此。

sentences.en: Almost every event you experience feels different once you've experienced it than you imagined it would have beforehand.
sentences.zh: 几乎你经历的每一件事，一旦亲身经历过，感觉就与你事先想象的完全不同。

sentences.en: That's the part of our psychology we don't seem very good at anticipating.
sentences.zh: 这正是我们心理中不太擅长预判的部分。

sentences.en: Do I recall a study that you did recently which tracked people over the course of their lives
sentences.zh: 我是否记得你最近做过一项研究，追踪人们的生活轨迹，

sentences.en: and asked them how they imagined they would change in the future versus how they had changed in the past?
sentences.zh: 并询问他们如何想象未来的自己，以及他们过去是如何改变的？

sentences.en: You are remembering correctly.
sentences.zh: 你记对了。

sentences.en: We recently published a paper showing that when people are asked to predict how much they will change in the future,
sentences.zh: 我们最近发表了一篇论文，表明当人们被要求预测未来会发生多大变化时，

sentences.en: they underestimate it.
sentences.zh: 他们往往会低估这种变化。

sentences.en: Look, we all know 18-year-olds are crazy.
sentences.zh: 你看，我们都知道18岁的孩子很疯狂。

sentences.en: They think they are who they are.
sentences.zh: 他们认为自己就是现在的样子。

sentences.en: They're going to be that way forever.
sentences.zh: 他们觉得会永远保持这样。

sentences.en: They have crazy hairstyles and tattoos that they believe they're going to want for the rest of their lives.
sentences.zh: 他们留着疯狂的发型，纹着他们认为余生都会喜欢的纹身。

sentences.en: And old people like me snicker and go, you're going to see.
sentences.zh: 而像我这样的老年人会窃笑，心想：走着瞧吧。

sentences.en: Because 18-year-olds underestimate how different they're going to be when they're 28.
sentences.zh: 因为18岁的孩子低估了他们到28岁时会有多大的不同。

sentences.en: And we showed this in our experiment by asking 18-year-olds to tell us how much they would change in the next 10 years
sentences.zh: 我们在实验中展示了这一点，让18岁的年轻人告诉我们他们未来10年会有多大变化，

sentences.en: and asking 28-year-olds to tell us how much they had changed in the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 并让28岁的人告诉我们他们过去10年发生了多大变化。

sentences.en: In a perfectly rational world, those numbers would be the same and they weren't.
sentences.zh: 在一个完全理性的世界里，这些数字应该是一样的，但事实并非如此。

sentences.en: 18-year-olds thought they would change very little.
sentences.zh: 18岁的人认为自己变化很小。

sentences.en: 28-year-olds reported having changed a lot.
sentences.zh: 28岁的人则表示自己改变了很多。

sentences.en: But what's so interesting about the study is it's also true with 58-year-olds and 68-year-olds.
sentences.zh: 但这项研究最有趣的地方在于，对于58岁和68岁的人来说也是如此。

sentences.en: That is, 58-year-olds think, okay, I'm done.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，58岁的人会想，好吧，我定型了。

sentences.en: I'm cooked.
sentences.zh: 我的人生就这样了。

sentences.en: It'll just be me, maybe a little flabbier, more wrinkles.
sentences.zh: 以后还是我，可能稍微胖点，皱纹多点。

sentences.en: But I'm the guy I'm going to be.
sentences.zh: 但我就是我，不会再变了。

sentences.en: 68-year-olds look back to the last 10 years and say, wow, have I changed.
sentences.zh: 而68岁的人回顾过去10年时会说，哇，我改变了好多。

sentences.en: So what's really fascinating about this, Dan, is that no matter how many times we experience these errors in our lives
sentences.zh: 所以，Dan，这最令人着迷的地方在于，无论我们在生活中经历多少次这样的错误，

sentences.en: and how many times we make the same mistakes, somehow we don't learn from them
sentences.zh: 无论我们犯过多少次同样的错误，我们似乎都无法从中吸取教训，

sentences.en: and we're left with the same confidence that we had before that now, this time, when I predict the future, I'm going to be right.
sentences.zh: 我们依然像以前一样自信，觉得这一次，当我预测未来时，我一定会是对的。

sentences.en: There are two kinds of errors.
sentences.zh: 错误有两种。

sentences.en: Sometimes you're driving someplace and you take the wrong route.
sentences.zh: 有时你开车去某地，走错了路。

sentences.en: The next time you always get it right.
sentences.zh: 下一次你就总能走对。

sentences.en: But then there are errors that are more like, oh, optical illusions.
sentences.zh: 但还有一种错误，更像是视觉错觉。

sentences.en: You know, you see those two parallel lines on the page and you say, gosh, they don't look parallel to me.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你在纸上看到那两条平行线，你会说，天哪，它们看起来不平行啊。

sentences.en: And then you measure them and they are, but then you stand back and they don't look that way.
sentences.zh: 然后你测量它们，发现它们确实是平行的，但当你退后一步看，它们看起来又不平行了。

sentences.en: So you measure them again, but they are, but they keep not looking that way.
sentences.zh: 于是你再测量一次，它们确实是平行的，但看起来还是不平行。

sentences.en: I think the kinds of errors we're talking about are a little bit more like optical illusions.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们讨论的这类错误更像是视觉错觉。

sentences.en: You can't help but see the future in this deficient way.
sentences.zh: 你无法控制自己以这种有缺陷的方式去看待未来。

sentences.en: Time and time again, you will find your predictions were wrong.
sentences.zh: 一次又一次，你会发现你的预测是错的。

sentences.en: And time and time again, you'll make the same predictions.
sentences.zh: 但一次又一次，你还是会做出同样的预测。

sentences.en: When we come back, I'm going to ask Dan how we can use insights from his research
sentences.zh: 回来后，我要问问Dan，我们如何利用他研究中的见解，

sentences.en: to help us make decisions that are more likely to make us happier in the future.
sentences.zh: 来帮助我们做出更有可能让我们未来更快乐的决定。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收看。

sentences.en: I asked Dan to tell me whether he's found ways to help people use their imaginations
sentences.zh: 我请Dan告诉我，他是否找到了帮助人们利用想象力，

sentences.en: to make better decisions for their future selves.
sentences.zh: 为未来的自己做出更好决策的方法。

sentences.en: We and many others have spent decades trying to figure out
sentences.zh: 我们和其他许多人已经花了数十年时间试图弄清楚，

sentences.en: how can we make human imagination better?
sentences.zh: 我们该如何改善人类的想象力？

sentences.en: If when people look into the future, they make mistakes,
sentences.zh: 如果人们在展望未来时会犯错，

sentences.en: what kind of training could we give them so they don't make these mistakes?
sentences.zh: 我们能给他们什么样的训练，让他们不再犯这些错误？

sentences.en: And I will give you the summary of 15 years of research.
sentences.zh: 我可以给你总结一下15年的研究成果。

sentences.en: It doesn't work.
sentences.zh: 没用。

sentences.en: Almost nothing anybody has ever tried makes a long-lasting, broad difference.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有人尝试过的方法能带来持久、广泛的改变。

sentences.en: On the other hand, the best way to predict your future, we've discovered,
sentences.zh: 另一方面，我们发现预测未来的最好方法，

sentences.en: is not to close your eyes and use your imagination.
sentences.zh: 不是闭上眼睛发挥想象力。

sentences.en: There is a completely different way to figure out how you will feel.
sentences.zh: 有一种完全不同的方法来判断你的感受。

sentences.en: And that is to ask people who are already in your future how they feel.
sentences.zh: 那就是去问问那些已经身处你未来的人，他们的感受如何。

sentences.en: Almost anything you're imagining.
sentences.zh: 几乎任何你正在想象的事情。

sentences.en: Should I move to Hawaii?
sentences.zh: 我应该搬到夏威夷吗？

sentences.en: Should I become a trumpet player?
sentences.zh: 我应该成为一名小号手吗？

sentences.en: I wonder if I should subscribe to the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我想知道我是否应该订阅《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Would it be better to have a bagel or a biali?
sentences.zh: 吃百吉饼还是吃比亚利面包更好？

sentences.en: Almost any decision you're debating, large or small,
sentences.zh: 几乎任何你正在纠结的决定，无论大小，

sentences.en: many people have already made it.
sentences.zh: 都有很多人已经做过了。

sentences.en: And they've made it in both directions.
sentences.zh: 而且他们做出了两种不同的选择。

sentences.en: There are people who are doing the things you're only imagining.
sentences.zh: 有些人正在做你仅仅是在想象的事情。

sentences.en: And it turns out that if you can simply measure their happiness,
sentences.zh: 事实证明，如果你能简单地衡量他们的幸福感，

sentences.en: you can get a pretty good guide about how happy you will be in the future.
sentences.zh: 你就能得到一个很好的指南，了解自己未来会有多快乐。

sentences.en: One of the experiments that we did that demonstrated this most simply is we created a speed dating clinic
sentences.zh: 我们所做的最简单地证明这一点的实验之一，是建立了一个速配诊所，

sentences.en: where young women came in and they had a speed date with a young man.
sentences.zh: 年轻女性来到这里，与一名年轻男子进行速配约会。

sentences.en: And they were offered one of two kinds of information.
sentences.zh: 她们被提供了两种信息中的一种。

sentences.en: Either they could learn all about the young man before they met him,
sentences.zh: 要么她们可以在见面之前了解关于那名男子的所有信息，

sentences.en: they could see his photograph, learn his hobbies, find out about his likes and his dislikes.
sentences.zh: 可以看到他的照片、了解他的爱好、发现他的喜好和厌恶。

sentences.en: Or they could learn none of that and they could get just one piece of information.
sentences.zh: 要么她们可以什么都不了解，只能得到一条信息。

sentences.en: Namely, how much did the woman who already had a speed date with him enjoy it?
sentences.zh: 那就是，那位已经和他进行过速配约会的女性觉得体验如何？

sentences.en: Well, it turns out, first of all, everybody wants the first kind of information.
sentences.zh: 嗯，事实证明，首先，每个人都想要第一种信息。

sentences.en: The women in our study all think they're going to make a much better prediction
sentences.zh: 我们研究中的女性都认为，如果她们能了解那个男人，

sentences.en: of how much they'll enjoy the date if they can just learn about the guy.
sentences.zh: 她们就能更准确地预测自己会有多享受这次约会。

sentences.en: But what we find is that they're much more accurate in predicting their own experience
sentences.zh: 但我们发现，如果她们除了另一位女性的体验外什么都不知道，

sentences.en: if they know nothing except another woman's experience.
sentences.zh: 她们在预测自己的体验时反而要准确得多。

sentences.en: This woman is, in a sense, a surrogate for their future selves.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，这位女性就是她们未来自己的代理人。

sentences.en: And we call this method surrogation, using other people's experience as a guide to your own.
sentences.zh: 我们将这种方法称为“代理法”，即利用他人的经验作为自己的指南。

sentences.en: So there's a commercial application that basically is built on this idea.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一个基本上建立在这个理念上的商业应用。

sentences.en: It's called Yelp.
sentences.zh: 它叫Yelp。

sentences.en: Exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And there are a few domains in which we all know that we want to rely on other people's reviews, if you will.
sentences.zh: 在某些领域，我们都知道我们想要依赖他人的评价，如果你愿意这么说的话。

sentences.en: Movies and restaurants, those are the two big domains.
sentences.zh: 电影和餐厅，这是两个大领域。

sentences.en: Now, why are we willing to rely on other people in these domains?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么我们愿意在这些领域依赖他人呢？

sentences.en: Because we can't imagine for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 因为我们无法为自己想象。

sentences.en: I mean, if I say, how much do you think you'll enjoy the new restaurant?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果我问，你觉得你会多享受这家新餐厅？

sentences.en: You look at me and go, how can I possibly close my eyes and imagine that?
sentences.zh: 你看着我会想，我怎么可能闭上眼睛想象出那个？

sentences.en: When we have no information about a future event, we become surrogators.
sentences.zh: 当我们对未来事件一无所知时，我们就会成为“代理使用者”。

sentences.en: We're willing to listen to other people.
sentences.zh: 我们愿意听取他人的意见。

sentences.en: But if you offer folks even the smallest piece of information about a future event,
sentences.zh: 但如果你给人们提供关于未来事件哪怕最微小的一点信息，

sentences.en: they will take that over all the Yelp reviews.
sentences.zh: 他们也会选择那点信息，而不是所有的Yelp评论。

sentences.en: So let me ask you, you're going to decide whether to spend a lot of money to buy a movie.
sentences.zh: 所以让我问你，你打算决定是否花大钱去买一部电影。

sentences.en: Would you rather see the trailer or would you rather read reviews?
sentences.zh: 你是更愿意看预告片，还是更愿意读评论？

sentences.en: If you're like most people, you would throw out all the reviews by every critic and every Yelper in the world
sentences.zh: 如果你和大多数人一样，你会抛弃世界上所有影评人和Yelp用户的评论，

sentences.en: if you could just see the trailer.
sentences.zh: 只要能看一眼预告片。

sentences.en: Because you trust your own judgment in some ways better than others.
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，你比信任他人更信任自己的判断。

sentences.en: You feel if you could just taste 30 seconds, 60 seconds of the movie,
sentences.zh: 你觉得如果能先尝鲜30秒、60秒的电影片段，

sentences.en: you'll know if it's the kind of movie you like.
sentences.zh: 你就会知道这是否是你喜欢的电影类型。

sentences.en: But you won't.
sentences.zh: 但你不会知道的。

sentences.en: Other people's reviews are going to be great information about things like,
sentences.zh: 他人的评论对于了解诸如以下信息会非常有价值：

sentences.en: did the movie go on too long?
sentences.zh: 电影是不是太长了？

sentences.en: Did the plot get predictable?
sentences.zh: 情节是不是变得可以预料了？

sentences.en: Did God come out of a machine in the end?
sentences.zh: 结局是不是强行植入了神转折？

sentences.en: All sorts of things you'll never get from a trailer.
sentences.zh: 这些都是你永远无法从预告片中得到的信息。

sentences.en: And yet, if you offer people these two kinds of information, the trailer every time.
sentences.zh: 然而，如果你给人们提供这两种信息，他们每次都会选预告片。

sentences.en: So would you suggest that we should actually have Yelp for everything?
sentences.zh: 那么你会建议我们应该为所有事情都建立Yelp吗？

sentences.en: That we should be rating our friends and spouses and children and professors
sentences.zh: 我们应该给我们的朋友、配偶、孩子和教授打分吗？

sentences.en: all via this kind of distributed review system?
sentences.zh: 都是通过这种分布式评价系统吗？

sentences.en: Well, as a professor, I do get rated already.
sentences.zh: 嗯，作为一名教授，我确实已经被评价过了。

sentences.en: So there is a review system for me.
sentences.zh: 所以对我来说已经有评价系统了。

sentences.en: And at Harvard, we have a quaint tradition.
sentences.zh: 在哈佛，我们有一个古怪的传统。

sentences.en: It's called shopping week.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“选课周”。

sentences.en: And in the first week of school, all the students come in and they visit classes.
sentences.zh: 开学第一周，所有的学生都会来听课。

sentences.en: They don't choose their classes ahead of time.
sentences.zh: 他们不会提前选定课程。

sentences.en: And they visit them all to see 15 or 20 minutes of a lecture because they're convinced
sentences.zh: 他们会去听每一门课，听上15到20分钟的讲座，因为他们深信

sentences.en: and the administration is convinced that they can tell from 20 minutes of someone's lecture
sentences.zh: 校方也深信，仅凭某人20分钟的讲座，他们就能判断出

sentences.en: whether they'll really enjoy and get a lot out of the class.
sentences.zh: 自己是否真的会喜欢这门课，并从中获益良多。

sentences.en: What they're ignoring is a huge database of information from people who actually sat
sentences.zh: 他们忽略的是，这里有一个庞大的数据库，里面包含了那些真正坐下来

sentences.en: through the class for 15 weeks and have a whole lot to say about whether you'll enjoy
sentences.zh: 听了15周课程的人的信息，他们对于你是否会喜欢这门课

sentences.en: it or not.
sentences.zh: 有太多话要说了。

sentences.en: You can't convince a student to take a class that has great reviews if they didn't like
sentences.zh: 如果学生不喜欢第一节课的那10分钟，你根本无法说服他们去选一门评价极高的课。

sentences.en: the 10 minutes of the first lecture.
sentences.zh: 问题在于我们所说的“多样性错觉”。

sentences.en: The problem is something we call the illusion of diversity.
sentences.zh: 我们认为自己是独一无二的，认为别人的经历可能对我们有一点参考价值，

sentences.en: We think we are utterly unique, that other people's experiences might tell us a little
sentences.zh: 但参考意义不大，因为毕竟我们和每个人都不一样。

sentences.en: bit about ours, but not very much because after all, we're so different than everybody.
sentences.zh: 嗯，胡说八道。

sentences.en: Well, nonsense.
sentences.zh: 你和大家并没有什么不同。
